intro: Deadline week turned the quarterback market upside down, with Kirk Cousins heading back to Minnesota and the Rams carrying a new injury scare into Sunday. Pittsburgh and Cincinnati both come in at 6-2 for Sunday night, and Patriots and Lions open the weekend in Munich. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Vikings trade for Kirk Cousins on deadline day
top.dek: Minnesota sent a third-round pick to Las Vegas one day after Carson Wentz went 8 of 25 in a 23-6 loss to Buffalo. Cousins has 20 touchdowns and 8 interceptions this season. The Vikings have lost two straight after a 6-0 start.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Rams expect Puka Nacua to miss at least a month
top.dek: Sean McVay said Nacua sprained the MCL and PCL in his right leg and has turf toe, all from a hit on the last offensive snap Sunday. He is likely headed to injured reserve. Cornerbacks Jaylen Watson and Trent McDuffie are also out.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Myles Garrett makes his Rams debut count
top.dek: Garrett came back from two months on injured reserve with three sacks and a forced fumble against Washington. Two of the sacks came in the fourth quarter and helped end a late Commanders rally. He played limited snaps.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 18: Christian McCaffrey's games with a rushing and a receiving touchdown
top.dek: McCaffrey ran for a score and caught a 12-yard touchdown in the 49ers' 38-17 win over the Raiders. The 18th such game of his career is an NFL record. He has also scored a rushing touchdown in seven straight games.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Steelers visit Bengals with the AFC North lead in play
top.dek: Pittsburgh and Cincinnati are both 6-2 and meet Sunday, Nov. 15 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. A Bengals win splits the season series and gives them a one-game division lead. Pittsburgh won the first meeting 30-27 in Week 3.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills grind down Vikings, own AFC's best record

stories.text: Bills smother Vikings 23-6 on Monday night
stories.summary: Buffalo ran 79 plays to Minnesota's 46 and held the ball for 42:32 in a 23-6 win. Josh Allen threw for 234 yards, a touchdown and an interception, and the Vikings went 0 for 8 on third down. The Bills improved to 7-1, the best record in the AFC.

stories.text: Bills need their left side back on the line
stories.summary: Left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson sat out Monday, and wide receiver Joshua Palmer missed the game too. Backups Tylan Grable and Austin Corbett each gave up four pressures, and Allen took four sacks and 11 hits. Getting Dawkins and Anderson healthy is the top injury issue heading into the Jets game.

stories.text: James Cook carries the load in Minnesota
stories.summary: Cook ran 31 times for 107 yards and a touchdown against the league's top defense. Keleki Latu caught a 25-yard score for his first NFL touchdown. Allen also became the fifth quarterback in NFL history to reach 5,000 career rushing yards.

stories.text: 42:32: Buffalo's time of possession in Minnesota
stories.summary: The Bills kept the ball for 42:32 while Minnesota had it for 17:28. Three long scoring drives covered 247 yards, and the Vikings finished with only 178 total yards.

stories.text: Bills visit the Jets on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Buffalo plays at the Jets (2-7) at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch the offensive line, which faces a Jets pass rush led by David Bailey and his 7.5 sacks.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins fall to Lions as penalties pile up

stories.text: Lions beat Dolphins 19-9 at Hard Rock Stadium
stories.summary: Miami dropped to 1-7 with a 19-9 loss to Detroit. Malik Willis went 13 of 25 for 128 yards and an interception, and the Dolphins scored no touchdowns on three red zone trips. Jake Bates kicked four field goals for the Lions.

stories.text: Achane's torn ACL still shapes the backfield
stories.summary: De'Von Achane is out for the season with a torn ACL, suffered in the Sept. 27 loss to Kansas City. Ollie Gordon II took over as the lead back, with Jaylen Wright also in the mix. Rookie receiver Caleb Douglas has missed three games with injuries but played Sunday.

stories.text: Jacob Rodriguez leads Miami with 79 tackles
stories.summary: Jacob Rodriguez has 79 tackles through Week 9, seventh in the NFL and first on the team. Ollie Gordon II has 463 rushing yards, 16th in the league, and has averaged 83 yards per game since he became the starter.

stories.text: 11: penalties Miami took for 87 yards against Detroit
stories.summary: Five of the flags were holding calls. The Dolphins also converted only 4 of 12 third downs and ran for 77 yards on 21 carries, which kept drives from finishing.

stories.text: Dolphins visit the Colts on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Miami plays at Indianapolis on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS at Lucas Oil Stadium. Kicker Zane Gonzalez has missed field goals in consecutive games, so watch special teams.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Maye's three picks sink Patriots against Packers

stories.text: Packers hang 45 on Patriots in Foxborough
stories.summary: New England lost 45-27 at Gillette Stadium and fell to 5-4. The Patriots finished minus-4 in turnover margin, forced no takeaways and allowed the most points of the Vrabel era. They now sit second in the AFC East behind Buffalo.

stories.text: Knee injuries pile up before the Munich trip
stories.summary: Rhamondre Stevenson, Will Campbell and Ben Brown all left Sunday's game with knee injuries, and Mike Vrabel said MRI results are still pending. A.J. Brown, who has missed six games, probably will not make the trip to Germany. The team may activate guard Greg Van Roten from injured reserve.

stories.text: Drake Maye: 299 yards, 3 TDs, 3 INTs
stories.summary: Maye went 21 of 38 for 299 yards and three touchdowns, but all three interceptions came in the first half. He has now thrown three or more touchdowns in six straight games. DeMario Douglas added five catches for 102 yards.

stories.text: 187: receiving yards Christian Gonzalez allowed
stories.summary: Gonzalez gave up 10 catches for a career-high 187 yards, and Jordan Love had six completions of 20 or more yards. The performance was the worst of Gonzalez's pro career.

stories.text: Patriots face the Lions in Munich Sunday morning
stories.summary: New England plays Detroit (6-2) at Allianz Arena in Munich on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 9:30 a.m. ET on FOX. The Patriots lead the all-time series 8-5 and travel Wednesday, a day early.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Bailey shines, Jets collapse in Kansas City

stories.text: Jets fade after halftime, lose 35-12 to Chiefs
stories.summary: The Jets led 9-7 early on two Jason Sanders field goals, then went 2 of 12 on third down after halftime and lost to Kansas City. Geno Smith was sacked five times. Aaron Glenn called the result disappointing and said the team must go back to work.

stories.text: Garrett Wilson out with a concussion
stories.summary: Wilson missed Sunday's game with a concussion. Running back Breece Hall returned from injury and finished with 87 scrimmage yards. Blake Freeland, Joseph Ossai, Tim Patrick, Trevin Wallace and Nahshon Wright were also inactive.

stories.text: David Bailey wrecks the Chiefs' protection
stories.summary: The edge rusher had two sacks, three quarterback hits and two forced fumbles in Kansas City. His 7.5 sacks through nine games are the second most by a Jet since 1982, behind Hugh Douglas.

stories.text: 13: forced fumbles for the Jets this season
stories.summary: The defense forced three fumbles against Kansas City to reach 13 for the year. Rookie D'Angelo Ponds made his first career start and allowed no completions on 14 coverage snaps.

stories.text: Jets host the Bills on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: New York hosts Buffalo (7-1) at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The Jets need to protect Smith better against a Bills offense that leads the league in scoring.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens trade for Brissett amid a four-game skid

stories.text: Ravens send picks to Arizona for QB Jacoby Brissett
stories.summary: Baltimore gave up a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-rounder for Brissett and a 2027 fifth, per ESPN's Adam Schefter. Arizona covers more than half of his remaining salary. Brissett started Arizona's first eight games before the Cardinals benched him, and he is expected to start Monday against the Chargers. Derrick Henry said the team needs all hands on deck.

stories.text: Jackson's thumb injury leaves Baltimore thin at quarterback
stories.summary: Lamar Jackson is out with a thumb injury, and the team's recap of the Jaguars loss lists him on injured reserve. Tyler Huntley is reportedly done for the year with a toe injury. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano played Thursday with a heavy wrap on his right ankle.

stories.text: Henry passes Tomlinson while running the Ravens' offense
stories.summary: Derrick Henry carried 17 times for 57 yards against Jacksonville and moved past LaDainian Tomlinson for seventh on the NFL's all-time rushing list. He also took 10 direct snaps at quarterback. Justice Hill added a 65-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: 4: straight games under 14 points, a Ravens first
stories.summary: Baltimore lost 33-10 to Jacksonville on Thursday night, its fourth loss in a row. The offense has failed to reach 14 points in four straight games for the first time in franchise history. The Ravens also drew seven penalties, four of them false starts.

stories.text: Chargers visit Baltimore on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: The Ravens host the Chargers on Monday, Nov. 16 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN at M&T Bank Stadium. Watch whether Brissett, newly arrived, can settle an offense that has stalled for a month.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals win in Madrid, tied for the division lead

stories.text: Burrow sparks 34-17 win in Madrid, Bengals reach 6-2
stories.summary: Cincinnati beat Atlanta at the Bernabeu for its fourth straight win. Joe Burrow went 24 of 29 for 271 yards and three touchdowns, plus a rushing score. The Bengals now share the AFC North lead with Pittsburgh.

stories.text: Fairchild left Madrid with an undisclosed injury
stories.summary: Left guard Dylan Fairchild exited the Atlanta game, and the team was still checking how players felt after the win. Andrei Iosivas continues to recover from Week 3 thumb surgery, and the staff will reassess his timeline this week. Ja'Sir Taylor, Jalen Davis and Brian Parker remain on injured reserve.

stories.text: Chase piles up 155 yards on 10 catches in Spain
stories.summary: Ja'Marr Chase caught 10 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown against Atlanta, including 142 yards and a score on eight catches in the first half. Tee Higgins added five catches and two touchdowns. Evan McPherson hit a 57-yard field goal before halftime.

stories.text: 74.7%: Burrow's completion rate against zone coverage
stories.summary: That mark is the best in the NFL, and Pittsburgh plays zone on 84.3% of dropbacks, the fifth-highest rate in the league. The Bengals expect to see plenty of it Sunday night.

stories.text: Steelers visit Cincinnati for Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: The Bengals host Pittsburgh on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Both teams are 6-2. A Bengals win splits the season series and gives them a one-game division lead. Pittsburgh won the first meeting 30-27 in Week 3.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns plan to go back to Watson after OT loss

stories.text: Browns reportedly return to Watson despite Sanders' big day
stories.summary: ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports the Browns plan to start Deshaun Watson against Houston, even after Shedeur Sanders threw for 297 yards in a 23-22 overtime loss at New Orleans. Coach Todd Monken said he was proud of Sanders but declined to discuss the quarterback job.

stories.text: Watson cleared concussion protocol on Saturday
stories.summary: Watson missed two days of practice, returned Friday and cleared the NFL concussion protocol Saturday, but sat out the Saints game as an inactive. His clearance opens the door for him to start Sunday. No other Browns injuries were confirmed in the sources reviewed.

stories.text: Sanders throws for 297 yards in first start of the year
stories.summary: Sanders completed 19 of 31 passes for 297 yards and two touchdowns, including a 64-yard score to KC Concepcion and a 39-yard overtime touchdown to Harold Fannin Jr. His two-point try to win the game fell incomplete.

stories.text: 2.9: Judkins' yards per carry against the Saints
stories.summary: Quinshon Judkins rushed 15 times for 43 yards in the overtime loss and got stuffed from the 1-yard and 3-yard lines on separate drives. He had 11 carries for 25 yards against Pittsburgh the week before, and Dylan Sampson played more snaps in that game.

stories.text: Texans visit Huntington Bank Field on Sunday
stories.summary: Cleveland hosts Houston on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1:00 p.m. ET on Fox. Watch which quarterback takes the first snap and whether Cleveland's run game gets going.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Rested Steelers eye the division lead in Cincinnati

stories.text: Steelers come off the bye with the division lead in play
stories.summary: Pittsburgh sits at 6-2 on a four-game winning streak and travels to Cincinnati on Sunday night. A win gives the Steelers the head-to-head tiebreaker after their 30-27 victory in Week 3. Defensive coordinator Patrick Graham's adjustments are the main storyline.

stories.text: No Steelers injuries flagged coming out of the bye
stories.summary: Pittsburgh used its Week 9 bye to rest up, and previews of Sunday's game list no Steelers injuries. Running back Rico Dowdle is back after missing part of the early season. Official practice designations arrive with this week's injury reports.

stories.text: Warren leads the league at 5.9 yards per carry
stories.summary: Jaylen Warren averages 5.9 yards per carry, the best in the NFL among players with at least 50 attempts. He ran for 127 yards in the Week 3 win over Cincinnati. Aaron Rodgers has 1,871 passing yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions.

stories.text: 7.5: T.J. Watt's sacks lead the NFL
stories.summary: Watt tops the league in sacks. The Steelers also allow 18.0 points per game, fifth fewest in the NFL, and 305.6 yards per game, seventh fewest.

stories.text: Steelers visit Cincinnati on Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: Pittsburgh plays at the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Watch how the Steelers' zone-heavy defense handles Joe Burrow, who leads the league in completion rate against zone.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Stroud's five TDs flatten winless Chargers

stories.text: Texans hang 44 on Chargers behind a five-touchdown Stroud
stories.summary: Houston beat winless Los Angeles 44-22 in Week 9 and moved to 3-5. C.J. Stroud threw for 384 yards and five touchdowns, and the defense sacked Justin Herbert eight times. The Texans scored 28 straight points in the middle of the game.

stories.text: Montgomery and Blankenship questionable for Cleveland
stories.summary: Running back David Montgomery and safety Reed Blankenship are listed as questionable for Sunday's trip to Cleveland. Wide receiver Jaylin Noel is on injured reserve.

stories.text: Kayshon Boutte turns four catches into 125 yards
stories.summary: Boutte caught four passes for 125 yards and two touchdowns against the Chargers, including a 63-yard catch and run. He gave Stroud a deep target while the run game struggled.

stories.text: 8: sacks of Justin Herbert in Houston's 44-22 win
stories.summary: The Texans dropped Herbert eight times in Week 9. Herbert also threw an interception, extending his streak of at least one pick in every game this season.

stories.text: Texans visit the Browns on Sunday
stories.summary: Houston plays at Cleveland on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX. The Browns are 5-4, and Stroud is coming off a season-high 384 passing yards.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts keep Taylor, sell off the receivers

stories.text: Colts keep Jonathan Taylor through the trade deadline
stories.summary: Indianapolis will hold onto its star running back after fielding offers from several teams, including packages built around a second-round pick. The Colts did trade receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs to contenders, after moving Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner in October. Interim GM Ed Dodds is running the front office after Chris Ballard was fired Oct. 19.

stories.text: Six Colts questionable against Miami
stories.summary: Justin Walley, A.J. Haulcy, Akeem Davis-Gaither, Mo Allie-Cox, Jalen Travis and Jaylon Carlies are all questionable for Sunday. Receiver Alec Pierce is on injured reserve.

stories.text: Spencer Shrader kicks 59 and 50 yarders in the loss
stories.summary: Shrader tied Sunday's game with a 59-yard field goal and gave Indianapolis the lead with a 50-yarder. Dallas still won 27-23 after a late Daniel Jones interception.

stories.text: 10: interceptions for Daniel Jones, in eight of nine games
stories.summary: Jones has thrown a pick in eight of the Colts' nine games, including the last four. He has 1,722 passing yards and six touchdowns this season.

stories.text: Colts host the 1-7 Dolphins on Sunday
stories.summary: Indianapolis plays Miami at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS. The Colts are looking to end a five-game losing streak.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars load up with three deadline trades

stories.text: Jaguars add Davis, Bates and Godchaux in a deadline spree
stories.summary: Jacksonville made three trades on Monday, landing defensive tackle Jordan Davis from the Eagles, safety Jessie Bates from the Falcons and defensive tackle Davon Godchaux from the Saints. Davis cost a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-rounder. The Jaguars are 6-2 and chasing home-field advantage.

stories.text: Silmon-Craig questionable, two Jaguars on IR
stories.summary: Cam'Ron Silmon-Craig is listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Tennessee. Eric Murray and DaVon Hamilton are on injured reserve.

stories.text: Trevor Lawrence is playing clean football
stories.summary: Lawrence has 1,932 passing yards and 18 touchdowns with four interceptions, and he has not thrown a pick in his last two games. His 18 touchdown passes are tied for fourth in the league.

stories.text: 32nd: Jacksonville's run stop win rate through Week 9
stories.summary: The Jaguars' defensive line ranked last in the league in run stop win rate before Monday's trades. Davis ranked sixth in that category in 2024, and Jacksonville expects him to help the front.

stories.text: Jaguars visit the 1-7 Titans on Sunday
stories.summary: Jacksonville plays at Nissan Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX. The Jaguars have beaten Tennessee four straight times.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans ship Hooker to Buffalo before deadline

stories.text: Titans trade safety Amani Hooker to the Bills
stories.summary: Tennessee sent Hooker and a 2027 fifth-round pick to Buffalo for a 2027 second-rounder at the deadline. Hooker is signed through 2028, so the Bills get more than a rental. The Titans had not planned to move him before the deadline.

stories.text: Seven Titans questionable, including two linemen
stories.summary: Tackles Peter Skoronski and JC Latham are among seven Titans listed as questionable, along with Tyjae Spears, Carnell Tate, Jaylon Jones, Marcus Harris and Tommy Townsend. James Williams Sr. is on injured reserve.

stories.text: Cam Ward posts a career-high 304 yards in overtime loss
stories.summary: Ward completed 26 of 40 passes for 304 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions in the 43-36 overtime loss to Cincinnati in Week 8. CBS Sports moved him up seven spots to No. 25 in its quarterback rankings.

stories.text: 0: home wins for the Titans this season
stories.summary: Tennessee has not won at Nissan Stadium this year. Its only victory came Oct. 18 at Indianapolis.

stories.text: Titans host Jacksonville after the bye
stories.summary: Tennessee plays the Jaguars at Nissan Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX. Jacksonville won both meetings last season, 25-3 and 41-7.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos add Henley at the deadline, rest at 7-2

stories.text: Broncos buy Henley at the deadline
stories.summary: Denver acquired inside linebacker Daiyan Henley from the Chargers on Tuesday, less than an hour before the deadline. The price is a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth. Henley started 41 games for Los Angeles over three seasons and is in the last year of his rookie deal.

stories.text: Waddle and Moss clear concussions on the bye
stories.summary: Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and cornerback Riley Moss both left the Panthers game with concussions. Sean Payton said he saw nothing serious before the bye. Safeties Brandon Jones (hamstring) and Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) sat out the game. Denver has no timeline for any of the four yet.

stories.text: Bonitto's strip sack seals Charlotte
stories.summary: Edge rusher Nik Bonitto beat left tackle Rasheed Walker with 1:24 left, stripped Bryce Young and recovered the ball near midfield. That play ended Carolina's last chance in a 26-21 Denver win. Bo Nix finished 25 of 37 for 237 yards and two touchdowns.

stories.text: 5: straight wins for Denver
stories.summary: The Broncos beat Carolina for their fifth win in a row and sit at 7-2 going into the bye. They converted 6 of 10 third downs while Carolina hit 3 of 10, and the Panthers took 13 penalties for 119 yards.

stories.text: Bye, then the Raiders at home
stories.summary: Denver is off in Week 10. The Broncos host Las Vegas in Week 11 at Empower Field, where Fernando Mendoza is expected to be the Raiders quarterback. Watch how Henley fits into the linebacker rotation after two weeks of work.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs wait on Mahomes' elbow before Atlanta

stories.text: Chiefs roll the Jets 35-12
stories.summary: Kansas City scored a season-high 35 points, went 4 for 4 in the red zone and held New York without a touchdown. The 6-2 start already matches the Chiefs' win total for all of last season.

stories.text: Mahomes day-to-day with elbow injury
stories.summary: Patrick Mahomes hurt his throwing elbow on a strip sack by David Bailey late in the first half Sunday. He kept playing and finished the game. He is day-to-day ahead of Atlanta, and the Week 10 injury designations list him as questionable alongside Xavier Worthy, Jaylon Moore, Peter Woods and Mansoor Delane.

stories.text: Ken Walker tops 1,000 scrimmage yards
stories.summary: Walker scored three touchdowns and gained 143 scrimmage yards against the Jets. He now has 1,044 yards from scrimmage and 11 touchdowns, tied with Jahmyr Gibbs for the league lead. He is the first Chiefs player past 1,000 since Isiah Pacheco in 2023.

stories.text: 5: sacks, a season high
stories.summary: Kansas City sacked the Jets five times. Chris Jones and George Karlaftis took two each, and Ashton Gillotte added one. Jones now has 90.5 career sacks, second in franchise history behind Derrick Thomas.

stories.text: At Atlanta, Sunday 1 p.m. on CBS
stories.summary: The Chiefs visit the 3-6 Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The first thing to watch is Mahomes' availability and how the offense runs if he is limited.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Mendoza takes over as Cousins heads to Minnesota

stories.text: Mendoza named starter, Cousins traded
stories.summary: The Raiders traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota and named No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza the starter on Tuesday. GM John Spytek said Mendoza passed every test. Sources reported Minnesota sent a third-round pick to Las Vegas.

stories.text: Zuhn in concussion protocol after Santa Clara
stories.summary: Offensive lineman Trey Zuhn left the loss to San Francisco with a concussion. His status for Seattle is the open question on a line that now protects a first-time starter.

stories.text: Mendoza gets his first NFL start
stories.summary: Mendoza has thrown eight NFL passes, completing six for 48 yards in relief against New England in Week 5. He won the Heisman and a national title at Indiana. Coach Klint Kubiak said he exceeded expectations in practice.

stories.text: 6: straight games allowing 30 or more
stories.summary: The 49ers scored 38 and forced five second-half turnovers, and the Raiders gave up 30 or more points for the sixth game in a row. That ties an NFL record.

stories.text: Seahawks visit Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS
stories.summary: Las Vegas hosts reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle at Allegiant Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch how the Raiders protect Mendoza and whether the defense can end the 30-point streak.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers lose Henley, face Ravens on MNF

stories.text: Chargers fall to 0-8 after 44-22 loss to Houston
stories.summary: Houston gained 485 net yards against the Chargers, the most Los Angeles has allowed this season. C.J. Stroud threw for 384 yards. Jim Harbaugh said his team has no interest in giving up. The Chargers also traded linebacker Daiyan Henley to Denver before the deadline.

stories.text: Herbert's hand clears X-rays, McConkey day-to-day
stories.summary: X-rays on Justin Herbert's left hand came back negative, and Harbaugh expects him to be good to go. Ladd McConkey was active but did not play because of back spasms and is day-to-day. Justin Eboigbe, Cam Hart and Isas Waxter all hurt ankles, and their severity should become clearer this week.

stories.text: Herbert sacked a career-high eight times
stories.summary: Herbert completed 13 of 23 passes for 193 yards with one interception and took eight sacks, a career high. His 58-yard touchdown to Quentin Johnston ended a 37-drive touchdown drought.

stories.text: 8: sacks on Herbert, a career high
stories.summary: Houston sacked Herbert eight times, and Harbaugh pointed to the pressure as a reason drives stalled. On the other side, Houston became the first team to produce a 300-yard passer against the Chargers this season.

stories.text: At Baltimore, Monday 8:15 p.m. on ESPN
stories.summary: The Chargers visit the Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on Monday Night Football, Nov. 16, at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Baltimore is led by former Chargers defensive coordinator Jesse Minter. Watch whether the line holds up and who is available at corner.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys win ugly, face 49ers next

stories.text: Jones says Cowboys must learn to close games
stories.summary: Dallas survived Indianapolis 27-23 on Sunday, but 14 penalties for 153 yards let the Colts tie it at one point. Stephen Jones said the team is not finishing drives or games the way it needs to and has a long way to go on penalties.

stories.text: Ferguson and Locke out against San Francisco
stories.summary: Tight end Jake Ferguson hurt his knee against the Colts and will miss multiple weeks. Safety P.J. Locke suffered another concussion and is ruled out for the 49ers. George Pickens (hamstring) and Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) sat out Sunday and are being monitored for this week.

stories.text: CeeDee Lamb piles up 195 yards at Indianapolis
stories.summary: Lamb caught 10 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown, including a 44-yard score before halftime. Dak Prescott threw for 335 yards and two touchdowns, and Javonte Williams ran for 101 yards and the go-ahead score from the 1-yard line.

stories.text: 153: Penalty yards Dallas gave away against the Colts
stories.summary: The Cowboys were flagged 14 times and still outgained Indianapolis 508 to 271 and held the ball nearly 36 minutes. Dallas also lost two fumbles, and Brandon Aubrey missed a 50-yard field goal in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: 49ers visit AT&T Stadium on Sunday at 4:25 PM ET
stories.summary: San Francisco comes to Arlington on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. The 49ers are 7-1 and Dallas ranks 31st against the run, allowing 147 yards per game, with Christian McCaffrey at 457 rushing yards and nine touchdowns.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants host Commanders on Thursday night

stories.text: Giants win in Philadelphia, lead the NFC East
stories.summary: New York beat the Eagles 19-11 on Sunday, its first win in Philadelphia since 2013 according to the team. The Giants now turn to a Thursday night rematch with Washington at MetLife Stadium, where they will wear Vintage White uniforms for a White Out.

stories.text: McCarthy and Skattebo expected back Thursday
stories.summary: Coach Harbaugh said J.J. McCarthy (hip) looks like he will play and Cam Skattebo (hamstring) should be full go. Both were full participants Tuesday. Abdul Carter (knee, back), Malik Harrison (groin) and Colton Hood (finger) were limited.

stories.text: Rookie Arvell Reese terrorizes the Eagles
stories.summary: The linebacker finished with 12 tackles, three sacks and a forced fumble in Philadelphia. He is the youngest player to record three sacks in a game since sacks became official in 1982, and only the second Giants rookie to do it after B.J. Hill.

stories.text: 41.2%: Giants third-down rate through Week 8
stories.summary: New York converted 40 of 97 third downs, well ahead of Washington's 31.9%. The Commanders defense allows 42.7% on third down. Those figures run through Week 8 and do not include last weekend's games.

stories.text: Commanders at MetLife, Thursday 8:15 PM ET on Prime Video
stories.summary: The Giants host Washington on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. New York's defense ranks 10th in EPA per play, while Washington's offense sits in the bottom 12 of the league.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles drop seventh straight before bye

stories.text: Sirianni leaves staff changes on the table
stories.summary: After the 19-11 loss to the Giants, the Eagles' seventh in a row, Nick Sirianni said everything can be on the table. He added that the team will not change coaches or staff just because of the record, only for strong reasons.

stories.text: Hurts out after blood clots found, Baun hurt
stories.summary: Jalen Hurts is out after doctors found blood clots and will likely miss the rest of the season. Linebacker Zack Baun left Sunday's game in the third quarter with a back injury and did not return. The bye week gives the team extra time to heal.

stories.text: Joe Milton struggles in first NFL start
stories.summary: Milton, signed off the Cowboys' practice squad on Oct. 16, went 18 of 34 for 169 yards with a 66.9 passer rating. He took seven sacks, three of them from Giants rookie Arvell Reese.

stories.text: 6: Sacks the Eagles defense got and still lost
stories.summary: Philadelphia sacked Giants quarterbacks six times, five on J.J. McCarthy and one on Jameis Winston, yet the offense could not score enough. The Eagles are 2-7 after winning their first two games.

stories.text: Bye in Week 10, then Steelers on Nov. 22
stories.summary: Philadelphia is off this week. The Eagles host Pittsburgh at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS, after the NFL moved the game up from 4:25.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders need Thursday night at the Giants

stories.text: Commanders face a season-defining Thursday
stories.summary: Washington lost 20-13 to the Rams and now trails the Giants by three games in the NFC East. A loss at MetLife Stadium on Thursday would sharply cut the Commanders' playoff chances.

stories.text: Patrick doubtful, Burks and Moreau questionable
stories.summary: Center Lucas Patrick, who entered concussion protocol against the Rams, is listed as doubtful. Treylon Burks and Fabian Moreau are questionable. Dyami Brown went to injured reserve and Jer'Zhan Newton was activated.

stories.text: Jayden Daniels keeps the ball safe
stories.summary: Daniels threw for 274 yards and a touchdown against the Rams. He has nine total touchdowns this season, seven passing and two rushing, with no interceptions. In the first Giants game he ran for 103 yards and two scores.

stories.text: 12: Takeaways for the Washington defense
stories.summary: K'Lavon Chaisson and Nick Cross each forced a turnover against the Rams, pushing Washington to 12 takeaways on the year, tied for eighth in the league. The offense managed only 20 yards on 10 plays in the third quarter.

stories.text: At Giants, Thursday 8:15 PM ET on Prime Video
stories.summary: Washington visits MetLife Stadium on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. Watch how the line handles New York's pass rush, which sacked Eagles quarterback Joe Milton seven times last week.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears reach the bye on a four-game win streak

stories.text: Bears survive five turnovers to beat Tampa Bay 27-24
stories.summary: Chicago beat the Buccaneers on a 38-yard Cairo Santos field goal as time expired Sunday night. The win moved the Bears to 7-2 and stretched their streak to four games. They head into the bye in first place in the NFC North.

stories.text: Burden concussion and Stevenson thumb carry into the bye
stories.summary: Receiver Luther Burden left the Tampa Bay game with a concussion after catching seven passes for 97 yards. Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson hurt his thumb in the same game. Chicago is off this week, so no practice designations apply yet.

stories.text: Caleb Williams throws four picks, then wins it with one deep ball
stories.summary: Williams finished 22 of 37 for 279 yards and two touchdowns, but he set a career high with four interceptions. With the game tied in the final minute, he found tight end Colston Loveland for 38 yards to set up the winning kick.

stories.text: 2006: The last time Chicago won with five or more turnovers
stories.summary: The Bears gave the ball away five times against Tampa Bay, four on Williams interceptions and one on a Burden fumble. It was their first win in that spot since 2006. The defense and the late drive covered for it.

stories.text: Bye in Week 10, then the Saints at Soldier Field
stories.summary: Chicago is off this Sunday. The Bears host New Orleans on Sunday, Nov. 22, at noon CT (1 p.m. ET) on FOX. Watch how the offense cleans up its ball security after the break.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions pack for Munich on a four-game streak

stories.text: Lions grind past Miami 19-9 for a fourth straight win
stories.summary: Detroit scored one touchdown and four field goals in Miami and leaned on its defense. The win was Dan Campbell's 54th as Lions coach, which puts him alone in second place on the franchise list behind Wayne Fontes. The Lions now cross the Atlantic for a game in Munich.

stories.text: Linebacker Jack Campbell goes on injured reserve
stories.summary: Campbell hurt his neck in the win over Minnesota and remains hospitalized. The Lions placed him on injured reserve Saturday. Trevor Nowaske is expected to start next to Derrick Barnes and Malcolm Rodriguez.

stories.text: Jake Bates kicks four field goals in Miami
stories.summary: Bates hit from 28, 33, 40 and 43 yards. The 43-yarder gave Detroit a 10-point lead with 4:28 left. The offense gained only 271 yards, well under its 395.4 season average, so his leg decided the margin.

stories.text: 11: Jahmyr Gibbs scrimmage touchdowns through eight games
stories.summary: Gibbs ran 20 times for 74 yards and an 8-yard score against Miami. That touchdown was his 11th from scrimmage this season. He averaged 3.7 yards a carry on the day.

stories.text: Patriots in Munich, Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Detroit (6-2) plays New England (5-4) at FC Bayern Munich Arena. Campbell has said his team plans to be physical with the Patriots. Watch how the Lions handle the early kickoff and the travel.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Love and two 150-yard wideouts rout the Patriots

stories.text: Packers run past New England 45-27
stories.summary: Green Bay turned four takeaways into 22 points and committed just three penalties at Gillette Stadium. The win moved the Packers to 6-3 and set up a Sunday home game against Minnesota.

stories.text: Josh Jacobs has finger surgery, Edgerrin Cooper is done
stories.summary: Running back Jacobs broke his right ring finger and is out indefinitely. He has surgery this week, and injured reserve is possible. Linebacker Edgerrin Cooper is out for the season with a torn Achilles, while Zaire Franklin is nearing a return from a shin injury.

stories.text: Jordan Love throws for 372 yards and runs one in
stories.summary: Love went 23 of 29 with three touchdown passes and no interceptions, and he scored the opening touchdown on the ground. His scoring pass to Matthew Golden was the 100th of his career. Tyrod Taylor finished the game in garbage time.

stories.text: 171: Christian Watson's receiving yards, a career high
stories.summary: Watson caught seven passes for 171 yards, with 109 of them in the second half. Golden added 10 catches for 164 yards, also a career best. Green Bay had two receivers top 150 yards in one game for the fourth time.

stories.text: Vikings at Lambeau, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Green Bay hosts Minnesota (6-2) in Week 10. The backfield is the thing to watch with Jacobs out and Kaleb Johnson, who ran 11 times for 59 yards and a score against New England, in line for work.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Vikings land Kirk Cousins after a Monday night flop

stories.text: Vikings trade for Kirk Cousins on deadline day
stories.summary: Minnesota sent a third-round pick to Las Vegas for the veteran quarterback one day after Carson Wentz went 8 of 25 in a 23-6 loss to Buffalo. Cousins has 20 touchdowns and 8 interceptions this season. The Vikings have dropped two straight after a 6-0 start.

stories.text: Kyler Murray out with a Grade 2 hamstring strain
stories.summary: Murray, who won the starting job in camp, missed the Bills game and is week to week. Wentz also appeared to hurt his ankle Monday night. That leaves Cousins as the likely starter.

stories.text: Justin Jefferson held to 58 yards on 11 targets
stories.summary: Jefferson caught three passes against Buffalo, and 19 of his yards came on the last drive with Max Brosmer at quarterback. A screen pass he did not secure was ruled a Wentz fumble on replay. The Vikings gained only 178 total yards as a team.

stories.text: 2.3: Carson Wentz's QBR, the lowest of any starter this season
stories.summary: Wentz completed 8 of 25 passes for 81 yards with two interceptions and a third pass dropped. His 38 percent off-target rate was the worst in a game this season. Minnesota's running backs carried only 11 times on 46 plays.

stories.text: At Green Bay, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Minnesota (6-2) visits the Packers (6-3) in Week 10. Watch whether Cousins starts right away and whether Kevin O'Connell runs the ball more after saying he got too stubborn about balance against Buffalo.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons deal Bates, host Chiefs next

stories.text: Falcons trade safety Jessie Bates III to Jacksonville
stories.summary: Atlanta sent Bates, a 29-year-old safety in the final year of his deal, to the Jaguars on Monday for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder. A team source said the move does not signal surrender. Coach Kevin Stefanski said the club will not punt on the season, and the Falcons sit a half game behind the division lead.

stories.text: Pearce returns from suspension with a back issue
stories.summary: Edge rusher James Pearce Jr. came back from an eight-game suspension in Madrid but played limited snaps because of a back problem. He had been listed as questionable. The Falcons reported no other new injuries after the 34-17 loss to Cincinnati.

stories.text: Bijan Robinson keeps the league rushing lead
stories.summary: Robinson ran for 100 yards and a touchdown against the Bengals and added 147 yards from scrimmage. He now leads the NFL with 880 rushing yards. It was his first touchdown since Week 8.

stories.text: 12: Falcons penalties in Madrid, a season high
stories.summary: Atlanta drew a season-high 12 flags in the loss to Cincinnati, and several wiped out big plays or stalled drives. Stefanski called them too many self-inflicted wounds. Michael Penix Jr. still ran for 50 yards, his career best.

stories.text: Chiefs visit Atlanta on Sunday at 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Kansas City comes to Atlanta for a 1:00 PM ET kickoff Sunday, Nov. 15, on CBS. Watch how the Falcons line up a secondary without Bates and whether they can stay clean on penalties.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers fall short, face Saints for first place

stories.text: Panthers rally falls short against Denver, 26-21
stories.summary: Carolina lost its third straight when Nik Bonitto strip-sacked Bryce Young with 1:24 left. Todd Wash made his first start as interim defensive coordinator after the team parted ways with Ejiro Evero. A reversed interception on first-and-goal from the 1 turned the game for Denver.

stories.text: Cornerback room stays thin, Ekwonu eyes a return
stories.summary: Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are still out, and Akayleb Evans and Will Lee III did not play against Denver. Practice-squad call-ups Corey Thornton and Marco Wilson combined for five pass interference penalties. Left tackle Ickey Ekwonu is expected back this month.

stories.text: Darren Waller leads the Panthers with four touchdown catches
stories.summary: Waller caught eight of 10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown against Denver. His score gives him a team-high four touchdown receptions. Young finished 28 of 39 for 276 yards and three touchdowns.

stories.text: 119: penalty yards on 13 Carolina flags
stories.summary: The Panthers took 13 penalties for 119 yards against Denver, and pass interference calls on fill-in corners kept Broncos drives alive. Carolina outgained Denver 353 to 312.

stories.text: At Saints on Sunday, 1 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: Carolina visits New Orleans at 1:00 PM ET Sunday, Nov. 15, on FOX. The winner takes sole possession of first place in the NFC South.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints win in overtime, host Panthers next

stories.text: Saints survive Browns in overtime, 23-22
stories.summary: Tyler Shough hit Juwan Johnson for a 15-yard touchdown in overtime, and New Orleans stopped Cleveland's two-point try after a late Harold Fannin Jr. score. It was the Saints' first home win of the season and left them 3-5.

stories.text: Shough plays through a broken left hand
stories.summary: Shough played with two broken bones in his left hand. Center Erik McCoy left during the 55-yard drive that sent the game to overtime, and the extent of his injury was not reported.

stories.text: Tyler Shough leads two late drives
stories.summary: Shough went 21 of 35 for 265 yards and ran 10 times for 51. He drove 55 yards in 50 seconds to tie the game, then 74 yards in overtime for the winner.

stories.text: 4: straight games with multiple sacks for Carl Granderson
stories.summary: Granderson sacked Shedeur Sanders twice and now has 7.5 on the year. The Saints say he is the first player since 2013 with multiple sacks in four straight games.

stories.text: Panthers visit the Superdome Sunday, 1 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: New Orleans hosts Carolina at 1:00 PM ET Sunday, Nov. 15, on FOX. The winner takes sole possession of first place in the division.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs fall to Bears on a walk-off kick, now on bye

stories.text: Bears beat Bucs 27-24 on a last-second field goal
stories.summary: Cairo Santos kicked a 38-yard walk-off field goal to end Tampa Bay's two-game winning streak. The Bucs trailed 24-13 after a pick-six, then tied it with a fourth-quarter touchdown and a two-point conversion. Tampa Bay is 2-0 in NFC South play.

stories.text: Mayfield three games back from thumb injury, Egbuka returns
stories.summary: Baker Mayfield played his third game since a dislocated right thumb. Emeka Egbuka came back after missing two games with a foot injury. Todd Bowles said the bye week is needed to get healthy.

stories.text: Bucky Irving rushes for two touchdowns
stories.summary: Irving carried 20 times for 97 yards and two scores against Chicago. Bowles flagged his workload: 111 carries over the last five games.

stories.text: 16: Tampa Bay's NFL-leading interception total
stories.summary: Zyon McCollum picked off two passes against Caleb Williams, and the defense forced five takeaways in all. The Bucs still converted only 2 of 12 third downs.

stories.text: Bye in Week 10, then at Detroit in Week 11
stories.summary: Tampa Bay is off this week and next plays at the Detroit Lions in Week 11.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Rookie Carson Beck takes over at QB

stories.text: Cardinals turn to rookie Carson Beck after QB injuries
stories.summary: Arizona placed Gardner Minshew on injured reserve Tuesday with a reported torn UCL in his throwing elbow. Beck, a rookie, will make his first NFL start Sunday against the Rams. The Cardinals had already traded Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore, and they signed veteran Josh Johnson and rookie Joey Aguilar as backups.

stories.text: Wilson out for the year with a fractured vertebra
stories.summary: Receiver Michael Wilson hurt his neck on the fourth offensive play Sunday after a hit from Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon. A source told ESPN he fractured a vertebra and will wear a brace for six weeks to two months. He is on injured reserve and is not expected to return this season. Minshew joins him there.

stories.text: Trey McBride keeps catching seven or more
stories.summary: Tight end Trey McBride caught seven passes for 54 yards in the 17-3 loss at Seattle. He has now caught at least seven passes in 11 straight games. He was also the target on Arizona's last fourth-down try. With Beck starting, he is the player the offense leans on most.

stories.text: 4 of 17: the red-zone trouble in Arizona's offense
stories.summary: Over the last four games the Cardinals have scored four touchdowns on 17 red-zone trips. They went 0 for 2 inside the 20 in Seattle, which had the league's worst red-zone defense coming in. The offense managed just three points and 166 passing yards from Minshew.

stories.text: Rams visit State Farm Stadium Sunday
stories.summary: Arizona hosts the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS. Beck makes his first start against a Rams team that has won three straight. Watch whether the Cardinals can turn red-zone trips into touchdowns.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Garrett returns, Nacua heads to IR

stories.text: Rams win a third straight behind Garrett's return
stories.summary: Los Angeles beat Washington 20-13 to improve to 5-4 after a 2-4 start. Myles Garrett came back from injured reserve, played a limited snap count and still produced three sacks and a forced fumble. The Rams now head to Arizona hoping to reach their bye at 6-4.

stories.text: Puka Nacua likely to IR with MCL, PCL sprains
stories.summary: Coach Sean McVay said Nacua sprained the MCL and PCL in his right leg and has turf toe, all from a hit on the last offensive snap Sunday. McVay expects him to miss at least a month. Cornerbacks Jaylen Watson (shoulder) and Trent McDuffie (back) are also out.

stories.text: Myles Garrett makes his Rams debut count
stories.summary: Garrett returned from two months on injured reserve with three sacks and a forced fumble against Washington. Two of the sacks came in the fourth quarter, the last one helping end a late Commanders rally. He played limited snaps, so the Rams can expect more.

stories.text: 70: Nacua's catches through seven games, an NFL record
stories.summary: Nacua finished with 14 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown on Sunday. His 70 catches through his first seven games of the season are the most by any player in NFL history. He also leads the league in receptions and receiving yards since Week 4.

stories.text: At Arizona Sunday, then a bye
stories.summary: The Rams visit the Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS, then take their Week 11 bye. Watch how Stafford spreads the ball around without Nacua against a Cardinals team starting a rookie quarterback.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: Niners force five turnovers, go 7-1

stories.text: 49ers bury Raiders 38-17 on a second-half turnover run
stories.summary: San Francisco forced five turnovers, all in the second half, to beat Las Vegas and move to 7-1. Jaden Dugger returned an interception 35 yards for a touchdown, and Fred Warner forced and recovered fumbles. Kirk Cousins threw three interceptions for the Raiders.

stories.text: Halton fractures ankle, goes to injured reserve
stories.summary: Defensive lineman Gracen Halton fractured and dislocated his ankle and will have surgery this week. Kyle Shanahan said Renardo Green (back) and Deommodore Lenoir (foot) are day to day. C.J. West and Deebo Samuel Sr. should return to practice Wednesday, while Mike Evans is not expected to be ready this week.

stories.text: Christian McCaffrey extends his touchdown streaks
stories.summary: McCaffrey ran 18 times for 68 yards and a touchdown and caught a 12-yard score. It was his 18th career game with a rushing and a receiving touchdown, an NFL record. He has scored a rushing touchdown in seven straight games, the longest single-season streak in 49ers history.

stories.text: 190: rushing yards, a season high on 43 carries
stories.summary: San Francisco ran 43 times for 190 yards against Las Vegas, its most rushing attempts in a game since 2022. Brock Purdy added a season-high 40 rushing yards and threw his 100th career touchdown pass in his 57th game, the fastest in team history. The Raiders gained 24 rushing yards.

stories.text: At Dallas Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: The 49ers open a two-game road trip at Dallas on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. Watch the run game and the defense's pressure against Dallas.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Lock steadies Seattle in 17-3 win

stories.text: Seahawks beat Arizona 17-3 with Drew Lock at quarterback
stories.summary: Lock started in place of the injured Sam Darnold and went 19 of 28 for 175 yards and a touchdown. Seattle improved to 5-4 and won its 11th straight over Arizona. The defense stopped the Cardinals on fourth-and-goal from the 2 late in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: Darnold out for Week 10, Lock expected to play
stories.summary: Darnold is out against the Raiders with quadriceps and rib injuries and could return after the Week 11 bye. Lock has an oblique injury and will be limited in practice, but he is expected to start. Guard Quenton Nelson is week to week after a minor knee procedure, and Leonard Williams has a stinger. Mike Macdonald said no one is ruled out yet for Charles Cross, Uchenna Nwosu or Rashid Shaheed.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba reaches 1,000 yards in nine games
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba has 1,036 receiving yards after nine games, the second straight season he has hit 1,000 by this point. He is the third player in franchise history with 1,000 yards in three straight seasons. He caught seven passes for 51 yards against Arizona.

stories.text: 2.41: Lock's average seconds to throw, his quickest ever
stories.summary: Lock got the ball out in 2.41 seconds on average, per Next Gen Stats. On throws under 2.5 seconds he went 13 of 18 for 110 yards, including the touchdown to AJ Barner. Seattle allowed no sacks and three quarterback hits.

stories.text: At Las Vegas Sunday, then a bye
stories.summary: Seattle visits the Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS. The Seahawks take their Week 11 bye after that. Watch Lock's health and whether Cross and Nwosu return.
